significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that an "information-source" residual-stream direction causally controls certainty and cross-language answers, while the effect varies systematically with "evidential obligatoriness"; this combines form (ii) causality with form (iii) ordering and predictive coupling between independently measurable quantities. It predicts that hearsay versus witness marking will order later certainty even after a language switch and that obligatory-evidential languages will show larger shifts, materially refining accounts of shared multilingual processing such as Wendler et al.'s 2024 finding of a common latent processing language. The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—"hearsay-marked premise[s]" lowering English-side certainty—and a causal mechanism; a clean null would support compartmentalization, although failure of only one of its three conjuncts would leave the composite negative branch ambiguous, so true and false are distinguishable but not maximally sharp. In the topic-substitution check, generic claims about shared versus language-specific representations would merit only the topic median; the evidential-obligatoriness gradient and cross-language source leakage are the claim-specific additions supporting a higher score.

reach.justification: The named handles are the compact "information-source" or "shared source direction" and its proposed steering or ablation, which could detect and suppress evidential contamination before the model produces its downstream answer, making the strongest handle ex ante rather than merely post hoc. Although the direction itself would need re-extraction for each model, the asserted relation survives recalibration: hearsay should reduce certainty across a language switch, with stronger coupling in obligatory-evidential languages, so a new model yields a predicted ordering rather than only another search procedure. The hypothesis ranges across multilingual LLMs, several language families, and certainty, hedging, and answer behavior; likely downstream users include multilingual-model auditors and developers seeking to gate or control source-sensitive outputs, though no deployment-ready screening rule outside this setting is asserted. Under topic substitution, broad cross-lingual transfer alone would remain a 5-level deliverable, whereas the before-answer source-direction intervention and transferable obligatoriness/leakage relation justify the higher reach.
